output.summary: An annual or perennial sedge native in some regions of the United States and widespread across much of the world, yellow nutsedge has triangular stems and produces hard underground tubers. The sweet, nutty tubers are eaten raw or cooked, but are generally soaked to soften them; they are also made into flour and drinks.
output.edibilityNote: The tubers are eaten raw or cooked, usually after soaking to soften them, and are also made into flour and sweet drinks.
